newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS - Issues to watch - Aug 15.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS - Issues to watch - Aug 15.

text.p: -- W.R. Grace gained a point in after-hours trading Thursday after announcing it would merge its packaging unit with Sealed Air in a deal valued at $5 billion. Sealed Air did not trade after hours.

-- HealthSouth Corp has offered to buy large pieces of embattled hospital giant Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp, the Wall Street Journal reported. HealthSouth made its offer after failing to receive a response to its $45 a share takeover bid for Columbia/HCA.

-- Loews Corp had $467.4 million of gross investment losses in the second quarter following a multibillion-dollar bet against the bull market earlier this year by the Tisch family, which controls 32 percent of the company's stock, the Wall Street Journal reported.

-- Eastman Kodak Co will put its name on up to 500 photo specialty stores across the U.S. within the next 18 months in return for the stores' stocking a full line of Kodak products, the New York Times reported.
-- ITT Corp late Thursday rejected Hilton Hotels Corp's revised takeover bid of $70 per share, or $8.3 billion, saying the price did not reflect ITT's inherent value.
-- PepsiCo Inc said after the bell Thursday that its board had approved the spin-off of its restaurant business, which include KFC, Taco Bell and Pizza Hut, to shareholders.
-- Allstate Corp said Thursday its board had approved a new stock repurchase program.
-- Coca-Cola Co shares rose in London trading after the company launched a new fizzy soft drink called Smart that is aimed at the youth market in China.
